utterances.text: No, not to the site. That was in the evening in the office. I think he didn't come to the site at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar please call up Exhibit P367, page 3, paragraph 1 of the B/C/S; and page 2, paragraph 7 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, can you see it? It's the first paragraph on page 3, and I had to count for the English version. The end of the second page and the beginning of the third page in English. You see the Working Group says that Sperlic came to the site and immediately told you to conceal things?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please show me the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Here it is. When the truck was pulled out ...

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct, except I can't remember whether he came on site or we talked in the office. I really don't remember, but I think this is okay. We did talk to him as to how we should conceal this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but when? That is important.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day when the lorry was pulled out and we established what was inside; and when the judiciary said that they were not interested, then we got together to see what we should do to conceal it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, why were the licence plates so important, which were not there as you say?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is rather important. It's unusual for a vehicle to move along the road without registration plates and then to be found in the Danube. It's an offence. If a vehicle is in traffic without registration plates, that's an offence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I must admit that I don't understand you. This is a truck that fell into the Danube. There's no windshield, there are no licence plates. You're pulling out something without a licence plate. He's no longer in traffic, he's no longer -- it's no longer operational. So why is it important because in this particular case this truck didn't have registration plates?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is important because there are some 20 people saw two human legs sticking out of that vehicle; that is important.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that can be important, but why are the registration plates so important? They're simply not there. So why is that important?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, I agree, it's not important. They're not there and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that you stopped work then and you left the policemen to secure the site?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with a patrol vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me what you did next.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to the police station in Kladovo, and we sat there, there were four or five of us, Sperlic, Vukasin; Milo Stevanovic; me; Nenad Popovic. I can't remember whether there was anyone else and we discussed the event and we discussed what we should do to conceal it somehow, to cover it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So is it right to say that it was your decision on that second day for the event to be covered up?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean me personally or the five or six of us?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, not you personally, but that you made such a decision in Kladovo?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after the district public investigator and prosecutor said that he was not interested in the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you take any other steps apart from that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After we had agreed, yes. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, I mean did you make any other -- reach any other agreements as to what else you should do?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I -- I compiled a telegram and sent it to the SUP in Bor indicating that there were about 30 bodies in the truck. That was my estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that it was also agreed on that occasion to find a larger crane?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because the crane operator said he could no longer pull the truck out because the ropes had snapped; and then we used some rollers, but it was very difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me who took care of ensuring the crane?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly, but I assume that it must have been the chief of SUP who called up the manager of the power-station, and then they agreed about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. A moment ago you were saying that the agreement was to paint over the door of the cabin and to attach licence plates?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the agreement was that we should paint it over and that we should cover -- to cover the inscription on the door, and to put on the truck Bor licence plates in the front and behind but to damage them so they shouldn't be too visible so that from a distance one couldn't see the exact numbers on the plates.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that with respect to these steps you did not inform the SUP in Bor?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the painting and the licence plates, no we didn't. We just sent this telegram to Bor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct to say that you returned during the night with the diver and did what we've just talked about, the painting and the attaching the plates?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So we've reached the point -- that is, we've reached the third day now, Mr. Radojkovic. When you arrived on the site, who did you arrive with? When did you arrive there? And what did you find there?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again I arrived early in the morning. I didn't even sleep that night. Let me add that I didn't even go home. And we waited for the large crane to arrive, and by the time the crane arrived it was about 8.00 or 8.30. It's a large crane of 30 tonnes capacity. We had to pull the truck out of the water again because the water had risen, and the back part was again in water. That is what I found and the steps that were taken were to pull it out again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is the gist of it that you had to move the truck further away from the water so that it wouldn't be pulled back into the water?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we wanted to move it further away from the water, to make sure if the water rises that it shouldn't submerge the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, Mr. Radojkovic, do you remember when you arrived at the scene whether you saw something that surprised you?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me try and refresh your memory. Am I right if I say that you saw on the road a truck loaded with a large number of coffins from a private funeral company?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but you haven't read it properly. I was already there when about 10.00 or 11.00 a truck appeared with coffins on it. I was already there. I arrived there early in the morning, and it was only later in the morning that this truck arrived with the coffins.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, all the things I'm asking you come from the official note that I'm quoting from, so I'll show it to you for you to check whether it is correctly stated or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Djurdjic, there is a matter that we need to discuss before this next break. I think as you're about to show the witness a document it might be better if we left that until after the break, and you can then carry on with your cross-examination. Perhaps the witness could be shown out now and we'll deal with the matter that has arisen and we'll continue again after the break. It will probably be about 10 minutes to 6.00 that we resume again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: A difficulty has been brought to the Chamber's attention which we've been trying to consider during this session, it concerns the next witness, a young lady, I don't need to name her. Unfortunately, she is in her final year of a course of study and must be back at her educational institution tomorrow and Friday to deal with an essential part of her qualifying to graduate this year. It had been anticipated on the timetable that she would have finished her evidence by now, and of course she hasn't started. She is -- has a plane booking that would -- for her to return to where she is living at 9.00 p.m. this evening. Because we are running late, this problem has arisen. In fairness to the young lady, it appears to the Chamber that it would not be reasonable to require her to stay to give evidence with the likely consequence that she would not be able to complete her course of study this year. So what the Chamber has in mind is that she should be released tonight to be able to catch the plane, with a view to her returning to be here on Monday, in the hope that at -- either at the beginning of Monday or during Monday we can reach her and hear her evidence at that point. Now, there will be another witness on the list who can give evidence in the meantime. We mention this to see whether there is any particular problem with this suggestion which either counsel sees. Mr. -- Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had discussed this with my learned colleague during the break, and we were actually trying to reschedule her flight so she could try to complete her evidence tomorrow and leave shortly thereafter. And I'm trying to obtain some information if that was done or not to see if we could proceed today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I can tell you that is not the case. She has a particular personal exhibition, and she has to prepare that exhibition, so she needs to be there all day tomorrow as well as Friday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of her personal circumstances; she had raised them in proofing. We had actually anticipated to conclude her evidence today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So do you see any problem then with it being fitted in at the beginning or early in next week, depending on how we go with the present witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If that accommodates the witness, that's no problem with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Most certainly, Your Honour. Were the witness's evidence somewhat different, the Defence would have no questions at all for that witness if her evidence had only to do with the circumstances that she experienced. Unfortunately, in her statement there are a number of issues on account of which the Defence has no choice but to ask her a number of questions. We do accept that she is unable to be heard today and that she has more important duties to meet. Any time she is back is all right with this Defence. The one problem that I have, Your Honours, is the next witness who has now been interposed, as it were. I would like to ask the Chamber to have the chief for this witness this week and then leave the cross for next week in order to give our Defence a chance to prepare. We are a little pressed for time. I must say that. I'm not sure if there is an understanding. The witness first announced for this week contained two names, the brother and the sister, Bogujevci, with the addition of Witness Radojkovic at a later date because his name had been omitted by oversight. There were no other witnesses that were scheduled for this week originally. At first there were two witnesses and then since last week a total of three. That is why it is a problem for us that the witness coming is not the one that was announced for next week, and we can't prepare for three or four witnesses ahead of their actual appearance. So could we please deal with K88 in chief this week and leave the cross of K88 for next week. That is our motion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just being informed by e-mail that travel arrangements for the next witness have been changed. I'm trying to obtain confirmation from that, but if that has been the case we could just proceed with her as has been originally scheduled. But I don't know if I have incorrect information or if there has been a change in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now. Could you confirm what you're saying. Our information only comes from the Victims and Witnesses Unit; we do not have it first-hand. If you could examine the issue and find out what can be managed without putting this young lady at risk of not completing her examination requirements. And could you please discuss that with Mr. Djurdjic so he knows. And if it is that she will not be here to give evidence tomorrow, would you please examine with Mr. Djurdjic the time that will be taken over the next witness in examination-in-chief. What Mr. Djurdjic asks is that we do not commence cross-examination until next week, the witness having given his evidence in chief. Now, at the moment that seems likely to involve the loss of a day's hearing, but if you could examine those issues with Mr. Djurdjic during the break. We will resume at five minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness has indeed been taken back to the airport and she will return home and will be brought back on Sunday to testify on Monday. The other witness that was to follow, Fatos Bogujevci, I understand that he is also going to be taken -- flown back home because he also is in the same situation. Both of them are students and are finalising their exams this week and in the coming weeks. We have agreed with Defence to have both of them on Monday and finalise their testimony on Monday so they can both return to their normal activities and to their studies. So tomorrow we will be proceeding with Witness K88.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And do you anticipate the evidence in chief of that witness will finish in one session?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: My colleague, Mr. Neuner can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If it's Mr. Neuner, we can be confident it will.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I am a little bit surprised by the situation to a certain extent, but I hope we will finish in one session, yes, Your Honour. It's one and a half hours as far as I remember for this witness, so -- which is a little bit longer than one session, but I try to complete my evidence in one session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, an hour and a half we can manage.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, we will manage, hopefully, in one session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I've got to make other arrangements with my time, that's all. Very well. Well, I take it then the position that's been reported has the concurrence of all counsel. The effect of it will be that we will not sit at all in this case on Friday, resuming after the evidence in chief of Witness K88, we will adjourn and resume on Monday morning to deal with two other witnesses and then go to the cross-examination of K88. Hopefully that will overcome the real problem that was facing the -- particularly the young lady, but it will also, I hope, provide some relief for you, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. You have fulfilled all of our desires.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. If the witness could be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, am I right to say that you did not attend the meeting that was held at Kladovo when the chief of SUP, Caslav Golubovic, arrived as well as the head of the OKP of the Bor SUP and the head of -- the chief of the Bor SUP and the head of the OKP of the Bor SUP?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. I arrived towards the end of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right to say that you took measures to secure blankets and sheets and all the other items necessary for the bodies to be individually carried across and placed in the other truck?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, someone else took care of that. I merely took delivery at the hotel of these items.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were the bodies arranged in such a way that they could be taken away for post mortems to be performed and all the other steps that needed taking?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, given what the conditions were, the best job possible was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Am I right to say, since that is what the official note claims, that it had become dark already and by that time you got going and started your work, all the preparations had been carried out already, it was dark already, and then you set about your work; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean exactly, what work?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Transferring bodies from the refrigerator truck to the truck provided by the utilities company.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that this work was in fact so hard that you could not continue beyond 2.00 a.m. and you stopped working?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was exceptionally hard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would I be right to say that you saw the truck being dispatched towards Donji Milanovac?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, am I right to say that because of the situation, meaning there was a war going on and the air-strikes and you were in a border area and just across the way from you was the border to Romania and they had allowed NATO forces to use their air-space, this being the reason for your decision to stem the flow of information in order to not disturb the public excessively, despite which all of the state bodies knew what was going on; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there's a state border there and on the Danube were Romanian military ships very close to the Arsa Bay. If they used a perfectly ordinary pair of binoculars, they were still perfectly able to see everything that was going on on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a very busy road, right? If any roadworks were in progress one would have had to stop all traffic first; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did say a while ago that this was in fact something we had to do, including bus traffic, the regular lines, and all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I now please have the usher's assistance. I would like to place on our screens an OTP document, 65 ter list 594.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you see the image there?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Wait a minute, please. It's bound to appear.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, am I right to say that this photograph was taken on day two, following your arrival on the scene?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably. I think the truck had been hauled back slightly to some degree already.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Slightly. It had been pulled back some way already. We can see now that this is a truck and not a container with no cabin attached?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that much is certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you agree this is day two?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I could agree to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have 65 ter list 00595.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you exhibiting this?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there were three photographs that were shown yesterday that were marked, and I would like to have that admitted -- I would like to have these admitted because they are unmarked; and if we could have this first photograph exhibited, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This photograph will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00040, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now 65 ter document 00595. We have it on our screens. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree that this one was also taken on day two?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You see that the rear of the container sticks well out of the water by this point?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I realise that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What about the third, or rather, my apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this different from the previous one?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The angle appears to be slightly different. All of these are OTP exhibits, so I followed the same order in which I had received these, as we see the truck gradually emerging from the water. I do not think it is of essence; nevertheless, perhaps this need not be admitted because the difference in angle is very slight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You would like this one as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Given the fact that the angle is nearly the same, I don't think it's of the essence, and I would like to withdraw my motion now. Can we now please, however, have 65 ter 596 shown on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, what we see here is the truck already perched on the edge of the river-bank. Would I be right in stating that this photograph was also taken on the same day?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said day two, right? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have this document admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this different from the present exhibit that was marked by the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The only difference is the annotation, Your Honours, but it was tendered in annotated version, with the witness marking the foot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's the same photograph that we presently have as an exhibit, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Your Honour, but this one is unmarked and the one shown the witness by the OTP yesterday was marked, we saw the foot a while ago that I had failed to observe. But my questions are moving in a different direction, and that's why I'm using the unmarked photographs. Actually, this photograph is an exhibit already, P361, Your Honours, admitted as 361, with the circle marked by the witness. It has been identified, and I don't think we need to enlarge the body of evidence. Can we now please have 65 ter 597, OTP Exhibit 597.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: While this is being done I just wanted to clarify that the pictures P361 was shown unannotated to the witness and the witness has marked in court the annotation. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, what about this photograph, was this one taken on the same day as well? You see that we can see certain openings in this photograph. Nevertheless, the forensic technician did a great job zooming in.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this one shows the crack in its lower portion, but the point of this photograph is to show the chain and the padlock on the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I do see that, but I'm talking about this being taken on day two before you broke the chain?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was taken on day two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have 65 ter Exhibit OTP 603.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You want this photograph as an exhibit, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Your Honours. I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00041, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radojkovic, what we see here is the door pulled more closely together with the screw -- screws and the sheet. There is no licence plate, and it's perched on the edge of the river, so this must have been taken on day two; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to have a closer look, please. Yes, this was taken on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we please have this admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: My memory is that we have this photograph; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we don't have this one as a matter of fact. There's another one that I have here and then the next is the one that we do have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. This will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00042, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have OTP 65 ter 598.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, what about this photograph, was it taken on the same day?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we please have this document admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00043, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I now have Prosecution document 600 on the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, is the truck still on the edge of the water, on the water's edge?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was this photograph taken on the same day?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: On what basis do you say it was not taken on the same day?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the inscription on the right side of the door is not there, and there's something else but I don't know how to explain it. At the latitude where Kladovo is I can tell by the shadow cast by the truck where the sun was. If you look at the previous photographs you will see that the sun was about to set, that means it was in the afternoon; and here, it's vice versa. This photograph was taken in the morning, because the sun rises in the east, of course, from the direction of Romania. But I could notice this on the basis of the shadow cast by the truck, so this photograph must have been taken the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But the truck is in the same position as it was on the previous two or three photographs.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be so. It depended on the changes in the water-level. When you asked me about the process of pulling out the truck, the last one with the leg was when the truck was still. This photograph was taken the next day, but it's possible that the water-level may have been slightly higher or lower.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that all these photographs that we've looked at, including those we saw yesterday shown to you by Mr. Neuner, were taken on the water's edge while the truck was there and not on dry land?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photographs of the truck were made while the truck was in the water and when it was pulled out. That would be my most precise answer because there are no more photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, on this photograph you see that the truck is still in the water, the front wheels and most of it is still in the water?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, but when I painted that truck I took off my trousers, and I entered in my underpants to paint the door, which means that the water was somewhere up to my waist.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But what I was saying was that all the photographs were taken while the lorry was partly on land and partly in the water?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that respect you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Witness, yesterday you told us in connection with the Timok review and its founder certain things and I wanted to ask you, you mentioned that he used to be your colleague. Do you know where he worked and why he stopped working?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He worked in the State Security Service, in Zajecar, and I know him when he came to Kladovo, and I don't know how he stopped working.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that the son of this person worked in the police?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know whether he stayed on working in the police and what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If my memory is right, I think he had some problems in connection with some gold. I think he left the service, but I'm not too sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And do you know that his son had problems because of human trafficking?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he had some problems with the law, but I'm not too sure about what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know that Mr. Radojkovic was a prominent member of the party Nova Demokratija in your region?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was never a member of any party.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't mean you. That's a slip of the tongue. I was referring to Mr. Vitomirovic.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. I know he was a personal friend of Minister Mihajlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. At least I know this from talking to him. I never saw them together, but he said that he was a personal friend of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know a person by the name of Ilija Matic?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I think he was chief of the SUP in Zajecar, I think that was his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Known by his nickname Ika Robija?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm familiar with the nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And do you know when Mr. Matic was appointed chief of the SUP in Zajecar?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps around 2001 -- no, no. The police station of Kladovo is not under the authority of SUP in Zajecar, but let me try and remember who was the chief before him. After 2000, anyway, he became chief, Mr. Matic was appointed chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: He was appointed by Minister Mihajlovic; am I right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And Mr. Matic was also a member of Nova Demokratija, though he changed parties before that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that. I wasn't in touch with him too often.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, these are just matters of general knowledge. Let me now take you back to a part of your testimony yesterday towards the end when you said that on the 1st of May, 2001, this article appeared in the Timok review and that it is of a journalist nature and that suddenly the entire Belgrade press carried it and public opinion became familiar with it, that this is rather important. Would you agree with me that this was planned and synchronised?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can just tell you my own opinion. Mr. Milosevic was already in prison by then, and suddenly reports appeared about Batajnica, Petrovo Selo, the refrigerator truck, Perucac, and I don't know what else, and all this was like a bomb-shell and it appeared on television and in the media, in the newspapers. My impression was that all this was -- that this was known from before but that the documents were kept in a drawer, they were pulled out of the drawer, and by synchronised action, all of this was published to create a certain impression among the people to undermine the integrity of Mr. Milosevic so that he could be expedited to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right if I say that apart from this inscription in the article, in the Timok crime review, which appeared in September, in 1999, that apart from the heading -- not the inscription, the heading, apart from the heading, everything else is just a journalist's story and that it is incorrect. It's like a newspaperman's -- a reporter's report?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would just suggest to my learned colleague, because he's switching here between two articles from May 2001 and from September 1999 that he has the article on the screen for the witness to read, and there are a couple of facts in this article and that he then puts some facts stemming from this article to the witness and then let's him make a comment as opposed to making here a broad brush about an article and switching from article to articles. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There is a possibility of confusion between the two articles, Mr. Djurdjic. If the witness is clear about what is in each, you may be able to deal with them without them being on the screen; but if the witness doesn't have a clear recollection, what Mr. Neuner suggests could be a way of dealing with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I told the witness what I was referring to, and he spoke about this yesterday that in September 1999 an article appeared under the heading: Refrigerator Lorry in the Danube and bodies, and that it had no echo among the public and the witness answered my questions about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So perhaps you can just tell me whether you had that article in mind when you were giving me these answers.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understood that you were referring to the article in September 1999, and I said that what prompted the article was okay but that it was more like a newspaper report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And the mention -- the only thing that is correct is the location, that it was close to the monument Koca Captain, the time is more or less all right but the rest of it is very free interpretation of his associates.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that article, the 1999 article, I didn't see it published in any other newspaper with a larger circulation in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Just one more question: Do you know at all whether the Timok review was distributed in Belgrade and other larger cities or was it circulated only locally?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in the Timok Krajina, that's why it was called the Timok crime review.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And you know who Cucuk Stana is?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that from history, it is the wife of Hajduk Veljko Petrovic, the Vojvoda of the first Serbian uprising; am I right? Yes, he waged war in my part of the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what kind of clothing Cucuk Stana wore?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like most Serb women in those days, kind of pantaloons, Cucuk Stana, a combination between a skirt and trousers, like most Serb women in those, days she wore "dimija" or pantaloons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Radojkovic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. That completes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you want to tender this lasting photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I did, and could it be tendered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00044, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, do you re-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, I would have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And, Witness, we can certainly finish your testimony today. First of all, my learned colleague asked you just a moment ago about the Timok Krajina. Could you tell Your Honours where Timok Krajina is in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Timok Krajina is in the east of Serbia, it borders on Romania and Bulgaria, and it includes the regional centres and districts of Bor and Zajecar. That would be the location of the Timok Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could maybe have again the 65 ter number 1.01 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm not sure,

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could scroll down a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: -- Witness, whether you can -- whether this map is big enough to encompass what you consider to be Timocka Krajina. Is it too small or is it too big?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We need more of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we then simply have 65 ter number 1 on our screens and we need to enlarge that certainly, but probably focusing on the same area, east of Serbia, which we had in the previous 65 ter map. Could we please zoom in on the eastern part of Serbia because that's how I understood the witness to direct us, east of Belgrade, please, could we just zoom in. Yeah, east, could we go a little bit to the east.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, you guide us. We just need to scroll to the right, yes.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be it roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you now with the assistance of the usher who will hand you a pen mark where the Timocka Krajina is.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we zoom in a little, please. This is the section that matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we can even zoom in a little bit further. I don't know if it's possible because the witness wants us to zoom in a little bit further.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is that better now? Or we can even zoom in further. Witness, you direct us.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is fine. This is fine. It's very difficult for me to be very specific and draw the border precisely, but I will try to give you a reference point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you could draw now where you believe that the outer borders of the region you describe as Timocka Krajina is.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand what you mean by the outer borders. Bordering on other countries or the Timok region?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Timok region within Serbia and if it also borders, let's say, to another state, if you could just mark the outer borders of the region itself, whether it's at the state border or within the internal borders within Serbia.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I believe what the witness marked is not being displayed. Maybe -- I don't see -- oh, yes, now I see. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not a large-scale map, really, and I can't read the names of the towns and villages, but this would roughly correspond to what you asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would seek that this map is being tendered, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00368, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And now I want to show you again the article about which my learned colleague has asked you a moment ago, and that is Exhibit 364. That's the article from the 16th of September, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And we need in the English version page 2, the first paragraph; and in the B/C/S we need from the right page, which is displayed here, just the left column, please, the left column, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It says here, the paragraph -- the relevant paragraph starts with: "A few days before ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In English it is the first paragraph, but I'm not sure whether the witness can read the -- thank you for English but for B/C/S: "A few days before the bombing started, a refrigerator truck ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you read this paragraph? Do you find it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We should move the Serbian article further to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we move to the right. I was misguiding here. I think what the witness means we need the left page of that article and if we could maybe scroll down --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A little further the way you started.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We would need to move to the left, please, the usher, and now with the last column here on the right-hand page down. Thank you. I think even further down. It states -- it starts: "A few days before the bombing started ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you find this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Maybe we can move up a little bit. I can also read it in the record if this helps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's fine. No, it's fine. Now I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It talks here about the truck. A few kilometres from the Djerdap hydro-electric plant the truck overturned and landed on the Danube river-bank, the door was slightly deformed, human bodies began to fall out. That human bodies began to fall out, can you confirm that fact to us, it's being accurately reported? I was asking you: Could you confirm whether the press article which states that human bodies began to fall out of a slightly deformed door, could you confirm that fact as being accurate? Witness?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This last sentence you read, I agree, but I can't agree that bodies were falling out. They were sticking out as if emerging from the inside of the container. If you say "fall out," that means it's out and down on the ground; and here what we had was something slightly sticking out, protruding, as it were. Therefore, my answer is the bodies were not falling out or were not beginning to fall out. There were bits of bodies sticking out through the crack. That would be the most accurate way of putting it, and my reply is merely in relation to the last sentence that you read back to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe this is not fine because Mr. Neuner started reading the beginning of the paragraph "several days before the start of the air-strikes ..." and then the text goes on like that. We should put to the witness the entire context, the substance of this piece, and not a single sentence and then the witness should comment on the context in its entirety as opposed to commenting on a single sentence. We have the Swiss plates here several days before the beginning of the air-strikes, a single truck, refrigerator truck, with Swiss plates was -- and then bodies falling out, and if that's something that the witness agrees with I'll be more than happy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You had a chance to do this during the cross-examination and I'm at liberty to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Neuner, do you see the clock?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I see the clock. I would be done after putting one more fact to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: About this article?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. It was suggested --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Then would you put to the witness the particular matter you wanted him to consider in this article, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: That's all I wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Another fact which is mentioned in this article, and that's the last fact I wanted to put to you, is that the crane came -- I'm sorry. It is reporting to a person -- to what a person said. He said he added that those were probably the bodies of the Kurds or the Talibans who had mysteriously arrived on our territory. Do you see here the information being reported in that article as being uttered by a person?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the copy is a little poor, but I do see that portion. I see the rest of the text as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What would your comment be on this information that a person who is quoted here in the article mentions that those were probably the bodies of the Kurds or the Talibans? What is your comment to this?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO RADOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No comment at all. I mean, I don't know. I don't know what the source is for this information, particularly if I go on reading, something about trafficking in human organs. There's a reference to Kurds here. This is the story that we released after the incident at Tekija. There is no other way I can understand this. It was a well-known fact to the public that some Kurds had come to grief. The Kurds, we refer to them as the Taliban. Further up from Tekija in a slightly different area. So it's possible that someone actually stated this on the record, but we do have to keep in mind the fact that this is a newspaper piece and that's all it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecution has no more questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chamber would make the observation to assist both counsel that it seems unlikely that it would ever be possible for the Chamber to place any reliance on a newspaper article of this type in reaching a decision in this case. I mention that because both counsel have spent quite a bit of time with this article. It is a report by a newspaper. We have no means of knowing or verifying the source of the information nor of verifying what is contained in the article. Counsel can expect that the Chamber will look to more direct identified and reliable evidence for any finding of fact that it makes, and I hope that will assist counsel in assessing whether they need to spend time on this or any similar type of material in the future. Mr. Radojkovic, we would like to thank you. You'll be pleased to know that that is the end of your questioning. We're grateful that you have been able to come to The Hague and for the assistance that you've given, and you will now be able to return to your ordinary activities. The Chamber will now adjourn, and we continue tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 5th day of March, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.55 p.m.,
